title: What a New Rebel Alliance Means for Congo
gist: Gbadamosi's Africa Brief reports that ex-President Joseph Kabila has joined the M23-led Front for the Refoundation of the Nation, which vows to challenge Kinshasa 'by all means', threatening to spread war in a country producing over 70 percent of the world's cobalt and undermining a Trump-brokered minerals-for-security deal. It also covers Mauritius riots, EU funding for eastern Libya, Ethiopia-Tigray fighting, Sisi's succession plan and Rwanda's F1 deal.

insights.claim: Former Congolese President Joseph Kabila joined the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation, an armed coalition including Rwanda-backed M23 and Corneille Nangaa's Congo River Alliance that seeks to challenge Kinshasa 'by all means, including force'.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
entities: Front for the Refoundation of the Nation
insights.so_what: A former president lending political networks to an armed movement raises the risk of the insurgency reaching Kinshasa.

insights.claim: The escalation shows the failure of the Trump-brokered Rwanda-Congo deal, under which Congo offered the US preferential mineral access for security support and Rwanda was to stop backing M23 in exchange for US investment in minerals processing.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: US minerals-for-security diplomacy has not held; supply risk to Congolese cobalt and critical minerals persists.
insights.locator: The escalation of the insurgency demonstrates the failure

insights.claim: Congo produces over 70 percent of the world's cobalt and holds deposits of other metals essential to technology and defense, and the conflict is rooted in competition over land and minerals.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Escalation is a supply-risk catalyst for cobalt and battery supply chains.
insights.locator: But on a broader level, Congo's conflict

insights.claim: The coalition's durability is doubtful given members' differing goals (M23 on Tutsi rights, Kabila on unseating Tshisekedi) and M23's reported internal power struggle.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Fragmentation risk could limit the alliance's military effectiveness and prolong low-intensity war.
insights.locator: Still, with opposition groups under one movement

insights.claim: Tshisekedi is weakened by calls to resign over constitutional changes that could permit a third term, Article 64 Coalition protests, and Belgian police raids tied to a mining-revenue money-laundering probe.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Political legitimacy erosion in Kinshasa raises governance and mining-sector risk.

insights.claim: Congo's Ebola outbreak is the fastest-growing on record, with nearly 10,000 infected and over 4,000 dead, no approved treatment for this strain, and spread to four other countries.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: A severe health crisis compounds conflict risk and regional contagion concerns.

insights.claim: Mauritius is experiencing its most violent protests in decades over living costs and water shortages, escalating after police shot a demonstrator on Oct. 9, with nearly 100 arrests including 16 minors.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Cost-of-living and climate-driven water stress are producing unrest even in stable island economies.

insights.claim: Ethiopia appointed a new interim Tigray administration after the TPLF withdrew from Mekelle, fighting continues across Amhara, Tigray and Afar, and observers fear an Ethiopia-Eritrea border war.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Renewed northern Ethiopia conflict adds regional war risk in the Horn of Africa.

insights.claim: Egypt's Sisi pledged to leave office in 2030 and proposed a 30-month military academy to train presidential candidates, while the military already controls much of the economy despite IMF loan commitments to relinquish some control.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: The proposal suggests a military-managed succession; the IMF programme's reform commitments on military business control are not being met.

insights.claim: The EU approved an additional 25 million euros for eastern Libya's Haftar-controlled authorities for migration control, on top of about $247 million allocated to Libya in 2021-2024, despite reports linking some officials to smuggling networks.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: EU externalization of migration control continues despite human-rights criticism.

insights.claim: Rwanda announced a 10-year deal to host an annual African Grand Prix from the early 2030s in Bugesera, drawing 'sportswashing' scrutiny from rights groups.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Reflects Rwanda's soft-power investment even as it is accused of backing M23.
